question: Should OpenClaw adopt this six-family taxonomy as a core, plugin SDK, Gateway, CLI, and Control UI contract now, or keep safety observability on existing diagnostics and plugin seams until the taxonomy and lifecycle are narrower and versioned?
rationale: The answer determines permanent public API, protocol, storage, trust-boundary, and operator UX contracts; repairing the current implementation cannot safely choose those product boundaries automatically.

options.title: Narrow and split the design
options.body: Approve the concept but require a smaller sequence built on canonical diagnostics, host-bound plugin authority, real session context, SQLite persistence, and live proof before adding operator surfaces.

options.title: Sponsor the full core contract
options.body: Explicitly approve the six-family public taxonomy and require versioning, compatibility, migration, privacy, and end-to-end proof for the complete cross-stack implementation.

options.title: Keep policy integrations plugin-owned
options.body: Retain generic core diagnostic seams and implement taxonomy-specific detectors, exporters, and dashboards as installable plugins until a missing generic API is demonstrated.

recommendation.title: Narrow and split the design
recommendation.body: Approve the concept but require a smaller sequence built on canonical diagnostics, host-bound plugin authority, real session context, SQLite persistence, and live proof before adding operator surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans core/plugin ownership, Gateway protocol, browser ownership, storage, and product surface boundaries covered by his recent architecture work.
